scope: Bounded independent local Docker creation, ownership, cancellation, deadline and cleanup review. All executed process replies are invented metadata.

independentControls.name: Cancellation during ownership inspection after acknowledged create
independentControls.observed: No start command; exact immutable ID removed; cancellation-independent cleanup confirmed; both planned cases remain errors and only one create occurs.

independentControls.name: Monotonic deadline expires inside ownership inspection
independentControls.observed: No start command; cleanup gets its own positive bounded timeout; immutable ID removed; batch remains timeout/error with one create.

independentControls.name: Cleanup identity substitution matrix
independentControls.observed: Each mismatch rejects removal, preserves cleanup-unconfirmed evidence and prevents the next case from creating a container.

independentControls.name: Name reuse between inspection and removal
independentControls.observed: Removal and followup inspection retain the original verified immutable ID, so a replacement object with the same name is never selected for removal.

sourceReview: Create is a distinct non-executing request. Only a full acknowledged ID plus exact ID/name/image/ownership inspection permits start.
Cancellation and monotonic deadline are checked after ownership inspection, before start.
Unacknowledged creation is never retried or started; absence alone does not confirm cleanup until creation has been acknowledged or a matching owned object has been observed.
Cleanup does not inherit the aborted execution signal and removes verified immutable IDs rather than names.
Unknown cleanup leaves an infrastructure failure and stops remaining cases.
Guest launcher retains the original absolute wall deadline and a relative cap; actual guest execution was not part of this independent review.
authorEvidenceSeparation: The runtime author owns delayed daemon-create after initial absence, unacknowledged-create and actual Docker/guest/parent-death tests. Those tests were not independently executed here and are not included in the ten-test count.
fixtureCorrection: Initial typecheck identified only a missing required assertArgsUnchanged field in the new invented FunctionCase. The fixture was corrected to false before final validation; no product defect is claimed.
limitations: No real Docker daemon, containers, candidate code, model/provider API, credentials, sealed corpus, or externally billed resource was used by this independent review.
Injected process responses establish deterministic state-transition behavior, not Docker daemon atomicity, actual cleanup latency, hardware isolation, or provider readiness.

Existing run-ID recovery listing can show current absence but cannot establish that an unacknowledged pre-crash create request will never appear later. This residual boundary was independently noted by the root and reviewer; no atomic daemon quiescence claim is made. The split lifecycle prevents that late object from being started by the failed operation.
The cleanup wait is bounded. An object created after that wait may remain inert and require later operator reconciliation; cleanup-unconfirmed remains an infrastructure failure.
Same-UID trusted-process interference and whole-daemon guarantees are outside this review. Source digests bind reviewed bytes, not the authenticity of external daemon behavior.
